title: Shard-aware result windowing & prefetch strategy for dashboard query APIs
creator: Diego Morales
description: Improve dashboard query latency for multi-tenant analytics by introducing shard-aware result windowing, tenant-prefilter bloom signatures, and a predictive prefetcher for hot time windows to reduce cross-shard merge and materialization costs.
background: Several customer dashboards that aggregate across many accounts see tail latency spikes during large time-range queries. Current approach fans queries to all time-sharded indexes, materializes per-shard top-k results, then merges which causes CPU hotspots and high memory use. Existing cursor pagination and caching improvements reduced average latency but tail P95/P99 remain above SLO for high-cardinality tenants.
approach: Add a lightweight tenant-prefilter using per-tenant bloom signatures (periodic job that emits active index shards and top-key sketches)
Implement shard-aware result windowing: estimate per-shard contribution to requested window and only fully materialize shards likely to contribute to the requested page
Build a predictive prefetcher in the query service that warms adjacent time windows for scrolling UX, bounded by tenant-level budget
Introduce an LRU-managed hot-index cache keyed by (tenant, time-window, query-template) with size throttles per-tenant
Add dynamic fanout control that reduces shard concurrency when merge cost predicted to exceed threshold and instead uses incremental merging with early-stopping
acceptance_criteria: P95 dashboard query latency for 30d-range, high-cardinality tenants reduced by >=15% in production canary
P99 reduced by >=10% without increasing average CPU by more than 5%
No correctness regressions: paginated results must remain deterministic and cursor-compatible with existing clients
Feature gated behind runtime flags and opt-in per-tenant rollout via console
Automated perf test integrated into CI using recorded traffic replay
tradeoffs: Bloom signatures add a small eventual-consistency window where recently active shards may not be included; falls back to conservative fanout when uncertain
LRU hot-index cache consumes memory on query nodes; enforced per-tenant caps to avoid noisy-neighbor issues
Predictive prefetching may increase request count (and cost) for tenants with erratic scrolling patterns; bounded budget mitigates impact
progress_updates: 2025-03-01: Design doc shared with infra and product for feedback; initial concerns about cache sizing raised by infra.
2025-03-04: Prototype bloom signature emitter implemented as a streaming job; accuracy at 99% for active shard detection in synthetic tests.
2025-03-07: Implemented windowing estimator in query service; local benchmarks show 12% P95 reduction on replayed traffic for a 30d window.
2025-03-10: Integration test added to CI to replay high-cardinality tenant scenario; flagged a race between cache eviction and merge optimizer.
2025-03-12: Fixed eviction race by moving eviction to a background coordinator; preparing canary rollout config and runtime flags.
notes: Baseline (prod replay): P95=420ms, P99=1.3s for target tenant cohort
Memory budget: initial cache budget 4GB per query-pool node, with tenant max 200MB
Safety: fallback path is full fanout merge if bloom confidence < 0.6
